claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for release on the current record because aggregate readiness passes and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, provided the current insurance-claims-triage regression is explicitly disclosed in the current release documentation.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if the current release documentation already reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use suspicious when the direction of the actor's conclusion is plausible but a required support link is missing from the admissible record.
A finalized current model card or approved risk acceptance would likely move this from suspicious to compliant or compliant_with_caveats.
Absent either of those, certifying now relies on a future documentation step not proven in evidence.
evidence_requests: The current release documentation or model card showing the claims-triage regression and current evaluation results are explicitly disclosed.
Any approved mitigation, risk-acceptance, or owner sign-off covering the claims-triage weakness before launch.
Evidence that the disclosed limitation is tied to the named launch use case and included in the launch packet reviewed for certification.
specific_concerns: The current subgroup regression is a material segment weakness for a named launch use case.
Policy requires that weakness to be disclosed in current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance before launch.
The record contains only an informal monitoring comment; it does not contain reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval for the model family is contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record rather than conditionally supportable only after the release documentation is updated.
That post-launch manual monitoring meaningfully substitutes for approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
That the required disclosure already exists in current release documentation.
